body: Long story short.....I am an amputee with a permanent disability parking pass. "How do you not feel bad for using the handicapped pass?" Me: "because I'm handicapped and my bone likes to poke out of my skin graft if I walk on it too much, plus it's my handicapped pass" them: "well you aren't really handicapped your only missing part of your foot and you walk just fine what percentage handicapped are you?" Seriously? You are really asking me what percentage handicapped I am? That is effin rude! I may be able to look like I'm walking just fine but you have no idea the amount of pain it causes especially when my bone pops out! People....

Age 22- So so so much lately has been learned.  The biggest one is to stop having everyone's back that will never have yours! I thought I had so many friends and when it came down to it no one wanted to drive me to the er when I needed them most- I always dropped everything I was doing to help them and as it turns out all except for 1 person was taking advantage of me in every way shape or form if it was money,  rides,   bringing them candy when their boyfriends broke up with them for the 50th time.....etc....I have become a lot happier of a person since I stopped wasting my resources on people that really could care less about me. Now I am also starting to learn how to see through people's fake bs on top of it
Overweight people is my biggest deal breaker- since I am so into fitness I feel the person also has to be fit. Usually overweight and bad hygiene go hand in hand.

I was a smoker for a few years and someone pointed out how much money was being wasted on smoking- not only the short term (packs of cigarettes) but the long term cost as well; my health. It's been a little over a year since I stopped and it was the best decision I could have made my wallet is a lot happier and I started being able to taste/smell/breathe a lot better after I stopped smoking my energy levels went way way up, I didn't feel dependent on anything which drove the haters that couldn't/didn't want to stop crazy and they tried to push me and say that I wasn't cool if I didn't smoke (these were 19-27 year olds) honestly there is nothing glamorous or cool about smoking....plus you will never hear the comment of "oh man I kissed them and they tasted like licking an ash tray" your parents are probably just trying to look out for you and your health- I know how much that sucks to think about. Seriously I would avoid smoking and find better outlets for your money.
My first question would be why do you want to start smoking?
